name: Planck length and the extrapolation that the semiclassical framework fails below it

published_statement: Burgess gr-qc/0311082 p.4: predictions 'must be made within the context of a low-energy expansion, in powers of E/M ... What plays the role of the heavy scale M in the case of quantum gravity? It is tempting to identify this scale with the Planck mass, M_p^-2 = 8 pi G ..., and in some circumstances this is the right choice. But as we shall see M need not be M_p'. p.25-26: amplitudes (3.5) suppressed by (E/M_p)^2 and (E/4 pi M_p)^2 per loop; 'the weakness of the graviton's coupling follows only from the low-energy approximations, E << M_p and E << m'. p.35: validity needs wavelength 'very small compared with the local radius of curvature'. p.46: leading quantum corrections 'controlled by the ratio l_p^2/r^2, where l_p = (G hbar/c^3)^1/2 ~ 1e-35 m ... At face value it is only for separations comparable to the Planck length that quantum gravity effects become important.' p.38: semiclassical Hawking results hold 'provided that the black hole mass is much larger than M_p'. Garay gr-qc/9403008 abstract: 'The existence of a fundamental scale, a lower bound to any output of a position measurement, seems to be a model-independent feature of quantum gravity'; p.2: 'throughout this work we set hbar = c = 1, so that the only dimensional constant is Planck's length l_* = sqrt(G); also, irrelevant numerical factors are ignored' ... 'the distance between two events will have a minimum uncertainty of the order of Planck's length. This conclusion, which has been reached by means of rather crude arguments'; p.3 (Mead, restated) Delta x >~ max(1/Delta p, l_*^2 Delta p) >~ l_*; p.4: 'these uncertainty relations are low-energy approximations to what the full theory of quantum gravity would give'; p.17: 'the notions of distance, of causality and any other notion based on a metric structure lose their meaning at the Planck's scale'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Burgess): GR + matter treated as a low-energy EFT; control parameter (E/M)^2 with M the lightest heavy scale integrated out -- M = M_p (reduced, M_p^-2 = 8 pi G) only 'in some circumstances'; M 'need not be M_p'.
H2 (Burgess p.35): short-wavelength modes much shorter than the local curvature radius; slowly varying ('nice slice') backgrounds, adiabatic vacua for time-dependent backgrounds (p.32-38).

H3 (Burgess p.49-50): the all-orders power counting is NOT demonstrated for general curved spaces ('similarly general power-counting arguments are not yet given for quantum fluctuations about more general curved spaces') -- the breakdown scale is an estimate, 'not in serious doubt' but not proved.

H4 (Garay p.2-4): quantum mechanics + special relativity + GR combined by thought experiments; numerical factors of order one ignored; the bound is 'of the order of' l_*, derived from 'rather crude arguments' that are themselves low-energy approximations.
H5 (Garay abstract/p.17): 'seems to be a model-independent feature' -- a claim about approaches to quantum gravity, not a measured fact; no datum at the Planck scale is used.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the authors had: hbar, c, G and dimensional analysis plus thought experiments (Mead 1964 as restated by Garay; Burgess's power counting). What they lacked, and still no one has: any measurement at or near l_P -- the location of the breakdown is an extrapolation by construction (Garay p.2 'rather crude arguments'; Burgess p.49-50 'not yet given' for general curved spaces). The only numerical inputs that could have moved (G) have not moved (CODATA 2018 = 2022) and cannot move the crossovers in Planck units at all (R/l_P depends on Lambda only). Evidence either way on the missing datum: (a) toward a LOWER breakdown energy (larger length) -- Burgess p.4 'M need not be M_p'; if so, the tree's sub-Planckian crossovers are even further outside the framework, so the refusal strengthens; (b) toward NO breakdown (a UV completion within QFT) -- not read here (later-literature search unavailable), so this direction is OPEN. So: the authors did lack data, the lack is real and permanent at present, but none of the obtainable data moves the tree's conclusion; the unobtainable datum could move only the words 'outside the domain of the theory' and 'exactly', not the order-of-magnitude location of the crossovers.
grade_evidence: The extrapolation as published (Burgess gr-qc/0311082 p.4, 25-27, 46; Garay gr-qc/9403008 p.2-4, 17) is that semiclassical GR+QFT is expected to lose control at separations 'comparable to' / 'of the order of' l_P, with numerical factors ignored, the scale M 'need not be M_p', and the curved-space power counting not demonstrated. The tree's crossover_is_sub_planckian holds under every Planck convention tried and at the crossovers the required curvature is itself Planckian (l_P^2 G rho/c^4 = 1.056, 0.732), so the tree's central claim -- the Ford-Roman and Casimir crossovers lie where the framework is not trustworthy -- STANDS at O(1). It is NARROWED because the tree (i) uses a sharp boundary and a band test [0.1, 10] that depend on an unnamed convention: under the reduced Planck length Burgess uses, two of three crossovers fall outside the band (0.0614, 0.0738; z3 window [26.46, 2513] excludes Lambda = 9.98); (ii) says 'exactly where' against sources that say 'of the order of' and 'need not be M_p'; (iii) states the boundary with no status word though the sources call it an estimate; (iv) excludes a few-l_P EFT cutoff where Fliss et al. treat a Planckian cutoff as inside the EFT -- their own condition |8 pi G xi phi^2| = 2.518 xi at the tree's cutoff excludes it only for xi >~ 0.40. No datum has moved (G, l_P unchanged in CODATA 2022). Not WRONG: nothing here refutes the tree's structural finding; the Lambda-free spread 10.26 is exact.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner names the convention (non-reduced l_P) and the O(1) status as hypotheses, replaces 'exactly' with 'to within an order of magnitude', and conditions the NMC exclusion on xi (or cites a site where Fliss et al. place the breakdown at a few l_P independent of xi). To OPEN on the domain claim: reading later literature (species bound, asymptotic safety) that shows a UV completion keeping semiclassical control below l_P would turn 'outside the domain of the theory' into 'outside the domain of the perturbative EFT'. To WRONG: only a computed case in which a crossover lies well above the breakdown scale in every convention -- not found (FR needs Lambda >= 105.3, Casimir >= 72.95 to reach even non-reduced l_P).
